messages:
lina.support: ACME reported spikes in tail latency and intermittent 429s from their dedicated eu-west-2 pool starting ~09:12 UTC. They say requests slow down for ~30-90s and then recover. Seen on both generation and embeddings routes.
acme.ops: yes, happens during our nightly batch ingest around 09:10-09:25. Throughput drops, some requests timeout. We captured a few trace IDs: trace-0a1, trace-0a2.
omar.sre: can you paste a sample request/trace? also which pool id?
lina.support: pool: ded-eu2-acme-01. sample curl we used:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"gptx-8b","input":"test"}'
```
acme.ops: attached small log snippet (trimmed):```json
{"ts":"2026-03-15T09:13:02Z","trace":"trace-0a1","lat_ms":1200,"status":200}
{"ts":"2026-03-15T09:13:30Z","trace":"trace-0a2","lat_ms":5700,"status":429}
{"ts":"2026-03-15T09:13:55Z","trace":"trace-0a3","lat_ms":9800,"status":504}```
ryan.infra: looking at infra metrics for ded-eu2-acme-01 — I see short bursts where GPU SM/util stays high on a subset of nodes but overall cluster CPU is low. suspicious. Posting relevant prometheus snippet:```text
avg_gpu_util{node="node-42"}=96
avg_gpu_util{node="node-43"}=18
```
mira.mlinfra: that pattern screams noisy-neighbor on shared-node hosting. Are these MIG partitions identical across nodes? If some nodes have heavier MIG slices (e.g., 1g vs 7g) you can get uneven distribution.
omar.sre: checking node labels — ded-eu2-acme-01 is a mixed MIG pool: some nodes partitioned as 7g.1gb and others 2g.2gb for density. Scheduler may have placed more ACME pods on the few 7g slices by chance.
lina.support: ACME insists they were on "dedicated" but we do allow mixed MIG layouts in the pool for binpacking. we need repro steps to show contention.
acme.ops: we can run a synthetic burst load, 200 concurrent short requests per second starting 09:10:00 UTC. we will provide traces.
ryan.infra: doing quick check of autoscaler logs — I see scale decisions delayed due to instance launch throttling:```text
[09:13:25] scale_decision: +2 desired=8 current=6 pending_launches=2
[09:13:25] ami_launch_throttle: rate_limited, next_retry=09:15:10
```
ryan.infra: so during the spike autoscaler couldn't add capacity fast enough; combined with uneven MIG distribution -> a few nodes overloaded.
mira.mlinfra: immediate mitigations: (1) temporarily increase headroom (scale_target +2) for this pool, (2) pin ACME workloads away from mixed-MIG nodes, or (3) move them to a homogeneous 7g pool.
lina.support: can we do (1) and (2) quickly?
omar.sre: I can bump the desired count and add a placement constraint to avoid nodes with label "mig=mixed". Doing now.
ops-bot: created escalation ticket #INC-5678 assigned to infra-team, priority=P1, links: https://redwood.incidents/INC-5678
ryan.infra: done: scaled pool desired=10 (was 6). also set nodeAffinity to avoid mig=mixed for acme's deployment. should propagate within ~30s.
acme.ops: seeing improvement in first 40s, p95 down from 8.2s -> 320ms. thanks. :tada:
lina.support: leaving this open to confirm over next 2 hours, and we'll run a full repro with ACME tonight. follow-ups: (a) investigate autoscaler launch throttle root cause, (b) audit pool MIG homogeneity rules for dedicated tiers, (c) consider pre-warm/standby for reserved customers.
mira.mlinfra: filing infra follow-up: MIG-layout audit + scheduler bias check.
omar.sre: note for runbook: if pool is "dedicated" but mixed-MIG is enabled, prefer tick-box "homogeneous-only" for critical customers. add to PRD.
lina.support: ACME confirmed they want homogeneous 7g nodes. I'll coordinate contract addendum.
ryan.infra: closing immediate remediation, leaving ticket open for root-cause. :thumbsup:
